# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):

Read before each phase, between probes and before finalizing. Initial controller failures and300-second home stagnation remain valid historical evidence. Use only new post-repair records to claim resolution. Root owns the next preview lifetime; after full verify/build report readiness here through verifier-progress.md and wait for root-owned preview-ownership.json to say running with the new build identity. The unrelated Paraform job released the heavy lock: fuser returned1/no owner PIDs. This is an observation, not acquisition. Recheck and acquire flock for headed hardware probes once root readiness and preview are current. No measurement while repair mutates source.

## Manual traversal check requested during repair review

The engineer's real-displacement test exposed that an early turn at the first common-route corner could leave `terraUnits` stuck at4. The controller fix is now requiring a true corner crossing. Independently check ordinary MANUAL following of the visible guide, including a small natural early turn and returning to the guide. Determine whether the player's proof recovers honestly or becomes permanently stuck despite subsequently walking the route. Do not infer manual usability from the now-precise movie rail. If it fails, capture body/progress/reference/support and first failed frame; route the observed runtime/proof versus signed-intent issue to root. Do not modify thresholds or predicates yourself.

Chapter clarified the manual-corner intent in `chapter-manual-corner-interpretation.md`, exact scene-v2 hash unchanged. It explicitly requires ordinary deviations and honest recovery without hidden frame-perfect corner coordinates; full ordered18/reference/support/body/arrival proof remains mandatory. This is an interpretation, not measured manual failure or source-patch permission. Independently check actual manual behavior and distinguish missing traversal from a stalled progress algorithm.

## Existing chapter:evidence tool integration notes

`main/tools/chapter-evidence.mjs` accepts the canonical server through `PARAVOXIA_URL`; use the root-owned preview so it does not create a duplicate. Its optional `--audio` path muxes the first supplied offline score render under the first Playwright video and cuts to the shorter stream (lines201–213). That produces a decodable AV artifact but does NOT by itself prove actual live cue synchronization or hearing. Label muxed/offline provenance accurately and keep any real live audio/cue timing proof separate. Do not claim this tool captured live browser audio when it used the WAV mux path.

# Independent story-verifier progress — 2026-09-05-after-the-hearth

Role: independent story-verifier. **No game-source edits.** All outputs live in
`verifier/` under this run. Actionable bugs are reported here and in
`verifier-findings.json`; root routes repairs to the single integrator.

## Phase P0 — preparation (survey + harness) — COMPLETE

Started while integration-v2 was still mutating source. **No measurement,
build, test, browser or capture was run in this phase**, and no source finding
is attributed yet.

Verified, read-only:

- Signed scene-v2 identity: live `scene-contract.json` sha256 =
  `4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e`
  — matches the commissioned signed hash.
- Contract shape: 4 beats (`ch13-home`, `ch13-return`, `ch13-survey`,
  `ch13-common`), 28 sync anchors (8 of them signed *contingent*), 17 guidance
  objectives, 15 mechanical checks, 9 evidence captures, 5 agency windows,
  9 shots, 6 score cues, 4 quality tiers + desktop/mobile/reduced-motion.
- Read: `CLAUDE.md`, `production-lock.md/json`, `verification-commission.txt`,
  `integration-progress.md` (v2 Phase 0 receipt), `main/src/story/ux/README.md`
  surface, `main/package.json` scripts, `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`,
  `tools/lib/evidence.mjs`, `tools/chapter-evidence.mjs`,
  `tools/chapter-journey-probe.mjs`, `src/story/JourneyRuntimeProbeBridge.tsx`,
  `src/story/ux/feedbackCues.ts`, `src/audio/sfxEngine.ts`.

Harness written (run-local, `verifier/probes/`):

| file | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/cgContract.mjs` | Reads expectations from the **signed contract bytes only** (refuses a non-signed sha). Extracts the exact state-conditional work orders quoted inside `variantIntent`. |
| `cg-preview-daemon.mjs` | The ONE owned preview. Builds once, serves that immutable dist via `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs` (free port, never 5174), verifies `<title>Paravoxia</title>` **and** pins the index sha256, writes `verifier/artifacts/preview-ownership.json`, owns child lifetime (SIGTERM / stop-file). |
| `cg-lifecycle-probe.mjs` | One long browser session per invocation against that one URL. Frame-stamped ledger of beat / objective id / marker label / work order / health / requiresMarker, signed-AV anchor activation, prompts, receipts, milestones, autopilot; before/at/after frames on every anchor change and every objective enter / silent text change; hashes every frame. Variant-aware (`--variant desktop|mobile|reduced-motion`, `--tier`). |
| `cg-reset-matrix-probe.mjs` | Applies the eight contracted reset triggers (`beat-exit`, `deep-link`, `replay`, `pause`, `quit`, `focus-loss`, `completion`, `sandbox`) and records objective/marker/health/AV/entry-cue state before and after each. `sandbox` is a plain load with no `?story=` at all. Unreached states are recorded `not-reached`, never as a pass. |
| `cg-preservation-diff.mjs` | Read-only drift classifier against `initial-source-hashes.json` (958), `integration-before-manifest.json` (74 + 40 absent) and `iterations/implemented-scene-v1-before-v2/source-manifest.json`, bucketed by the signed contract's 118 allowedPaths / 194 protectedPaths, recording each changed file's **mtime** so a concurrent unrelated refactor is not blamed on this run. |

Evidence-schema reconnaissance (so nothing is authored by template later):

- `paravoxia.objectiveLifecycleEvidence.v1` requires, per objective: exact
  contract kind/anchors/markerLabel/workOrder, `entryCount` ≥ 1,
  `markerObservations` ≥ entryCount all exactly equal to the signed label,
  `missingMarkerFrames === 0`, ordered `entered→ready→completed→cleared`,
  `feedbackEmissionsPerEntry` all `1`, presentation-only separation, four
  variant proofs bound to `variant-desktop` / `variant-mobile` /
  `variant-reduced-motion` / `quality-potato`, and all eight reset triggers
  exactly once.
- `ch13:return:launch` (`requiresMarker: false`, `targetMode: none`,
  `maxVisibleTargets: 0`) instead needs `tools/lib/guidanceTargets.mjs`
  evidence: per-entry raw observations carrying
  `controlId / controlAvailable / controlInputActive / boardedState /
  controlOwnership / presentedFrameId / sourceRevision / contractSha256`, zero
  directional markers, and a `control-input` completion with accepted fresh
  input and a real `controlStateBefore !== controlStateAfter` — an authored
  timed bundle cannot satisfy it. The harness records exactly these fields.

Harness self-checks done without touching the game: `node --check` on all three
modules, and `lib/cgContract.mjs` correctly recovers the two signed v2
state-conditional work orders verbatim —

- `ch13:survey:test` preparing state: *"W-7744 is preparing to test the offered
  route." / "Keep his approach clear. Follow his progress, or return to the last
  tested point to revise."*
- `ch13:common:reciprocal` preparation state: *"W-7744 is taking up the
  reference position." / "Give him room to reach it. When the guide appears,
  follow it from the survey end."*

Observability decisions (so no boolean is filled without a measurement):

- Objective/marker/work-order/health: production HUD data attributes plus
  `window.__paravoxiaJourneyProbe.getSnapshot()` (query-gated, passive).
- Anchors: `signedSceneAv` (`anchorId`, `anchorEvent`, `activationSequence`,
  `activationHistoryAnchorIds`).
- Entry acknowledgement counting: the runtime's own SFX queue trace
  (`window.__voxSfxTrace()` `triggerCounts.objectiveEnter`). This is a **queue
  observation, not a hearing claim**, and will be labelled as such everywhere.

## Gate status — WAITING (not yet measuring)

Both preconditions are required before any measurement:

| precondition | state |
| --- | --- |
| `integration-v2-invocation.json` → `finishedAt` | **absent** (integration still running; `run-integration-v2.py` pid 435684 alive, stream still growing at 08:55 UTC, started 08:30 UTC) |
| root's `verification-ready.json` | **absent** |

Polled at ≤45 s intervals. **No build, test, gate, browser or capture has been
run.** Harness is complete and idle.

Hardware: `/home/thomasphillip/Projects/Paraform/harness/output/.heavy.lock`
existed and `fuser` showed **no holder** at survey time. That is an observation,
not an acquisition — ownership will be re-tested with a non-blocking `flock` at
the moment a real-GPU probe starts, and never waited on blocking for >60 s.

## Preview ownership

None started yet. No preview server is running for this run at this time.

## Phase C4 — bounded on-foot diagnostics (root's 10:06 continue) — TWO BLOCKERS

Both runs used an **explicitly labelled prerequisite fixture**: one press of the
shipped ordinary disembark key (`KeyF`, the `surface`+`flight` handler in
`App.tsx`), applied only because the entry actually booted aboard the ship, and
recorded in `summary.prerequisiteFixtures` with before/after state. It grants no
milestone, position, progress or route credit. **Neither run is a cold journey
and neither is reported as one.**

### C4.1 — `post/survey-diag-1`: the disembark unblocks the approach, then a NEW blocker

With the fixture applied (`controlMode` flight → fps, confirmed in the record),
the chapter genuinely came alive:

| measurement | value |
| --- | --- |
| `anc.cg.repeated-measure` | 3258 ms, exact signed event text |
| `ch13:survey:offer` → offer performed | objective cleared, `anc.cg.demonstration-opened` at 13 780 ms |
| `ch13:survey:start` entered | 13 780 ms, exact signed label `Survey start · begin a route` and work order |
| player walked | **58.632 real units** (2643 pose samples), largest single-sample step 3.11 — no teleport |
| W-7744 | mounted and static at `[-34, 51.1, 10]` |

And then it stopped for the remaining ~286 s.

**VF-RAIL-2 (candidate CG-IMPL-006) — the ch13 movie rail can never begin the
survey recording.** The rail's arrival gates compare a **full 3D distance**
between the player's live world position and poses authored on the ground plane:

| quantity | value |
| --- | --- |
| player body y | 52.79–52.80 in **every one of 2643 samples** |
| `CG_POSES.S` | `(-26, 51.05, 12)` |
| minimum achievable 3D distance to S | **1.745** (horizontal 0.13 — she is standing on it) |
| rail gate | `CG_RAIL_START_AIM + CG_RAIL_ROUTE_ARRIVE = 0.35 + 0.35 = 0.70` |
| time within 0.5 horizontal units of S | 261 of 354 pose-ledger entries (~4.5 min) |
| rail state throughout | `routeAction: 'walk'`, `stillTime 0`, `teleportNudgesTotal 0` |
| live prompt throughout | `F | Begin recording your route` |

`0038-strip-ch13-survey.png` shows it plainly: the marker reads **`survey start ·
begin a route · 0m`**, the F prompt is on screen, the debug HUD reads `Flight:
surface / fps`. She is standing on the mark she cannot reach.

Why the prompt appears but the rail cannot act: the shipped resolver reach is
`CG_POINT_REACH = 2.0`, which 1.745 satisfies — with only **0.255 units of
margin**. Why 3026 passing tests cannot see it:
`commonGroundDirector.test.ts`'s `standAt()` calls
`setPlayerWorldPosition(point.x, point.y, point.z)` at the authored pose y, i.e.
**a body of zero height**, so every rail regression runs at a vertical offset of
0. This is exactly the integration seam the commission warned the unit tests
would miss. Gates below the live 1.745 offset: `CG_RAIL_ROUTE_ARRIVE 0.35`,
`CG_RAIL_POSE_ARRIVE 0.6` (offer-span at E), `CG_RAIL_START_AIM+ARRIVE 0.70`,
`CG_RAIL_CORNER_OVERSHOOT 0.6`.

**Consequence for the commission: the CG-IMPL-005 ordered-cursor repair is still
UNTESTED in a browser.** No route traversal was ever entered, so nothing is yet
known — good or bad — about retargeting the visited start, corner shortcuts, the
ordered 18 units, the long-vs-short route classes, first-try-legal long success,
the three cold journeys, the station→home→ch13 bridge, or the ch13 segment of the
full story movie. All of it sits downstream of an act the rail cannot perform.

### C4.2 — `post/common-diag-1`: two genuine positives from a synthetic state

Deep link + the same labelled fixture. Its survey prerequisites are **not
earned**, so this is a synthetic state that proves no journey.

- **Signed preparation copy is exact.** `ch13:common:reciprocal` entered showing
  the scene-v2 *preparation* conditional work order verbatim — "W-7744 is taking
  up the reference position." / "Give him room to reach it. When the guide
  appears, follow it from the survey end." — matching the array quoted inside
  the signed `variantIntent` byte for byte, under the exact signed marker label
  `Far reference · check my route`.
- **Body blockage holds, it does not displace.** With Terra's body 0.38
  horizontal units from W-7744, he moved 0.2 units and **held**; he did not push
  her, and `teleportNudgesTotal` stayed 0 — consistent with the signed rule that
  a player blocking his leg causes a hold.
- **To re-test after repair:** the rail walked Terra 60 units onto the reference
  itself rather than to the signed standby clear of E, and no anchor activated in
  145 s. From an unearned deep-link state neither is attributable yet.

## Status: TWO BLOCKERS REPORTED TOGETHER, awaiting root routing

`verifier-findings.json` → `blockersForOneBoundedRepair`:

1. **VF-DEEPLINK-1** — ch13-survey / ch13-common deep-link entry boots aboard the
   landed Kestrel (`controlMode: 'flight'`); `commonGroundRailPlan()` has an
   `exit-ship` branch only under `ch13-return`, so the entry can never recover.
2. **VF-RAIL-2** — rail arrival gates are unsatisfiable against ground-authored
   poses, because the live body sits 1.745 units above them.

No game source was modified, no threshold or predicate was touched, no teleport,
progress grant or timeout rescue was used anywhere, and no unrun check is marked
passed. The owned preview at `http://127.0.0.1:43617/` is root's and remains
running and usable for owner review; this role started no server and will orphan
none.

# Score interpretation — home-anchor eligibility

**Later eligible home anchors must remain usable on Continue or a valid deep link while the ineligible live install acknowledgement stays silent.** Suppressing the entire home-anchor sequence is not an interpretation of the signed hydration rule. This is a bounded interpretation of scene-v2, not a new direction, independent runtime acceptance or authorization to fabricate receipts.

Contract: `scene-contract.json`, SHA-256 **`4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e`**. Reviewed `verifier-findings.json#VF-ANCHOR-OBS-1`, its home/survey summary artifacts, and the requested source owners.

## Binding clauses

- `/syncAnchors/0` (`anc.cg.cell-installed`) requires the **actual live install receipt**, one consumed cell and at most one acknowledgement when a home score host is available. Its acceptance explicitly says a hydrated entry is steady and silent, consuming no second cell. `/score/cues/0` likewise permits no completion transient on restore and no listening gate.
- `/syncAnchors/1` (`anc.cg.home-steady`) explicitly restores the steady home variant on hydrated entry, without a completion transient or queued acknowledgement. Its real departed/restored receipts, on-foot Tidegarden and actual-core conditions remain required.
- `/guidance/objectives/0` enters at home-steady and states that **a restored save reaches the review objective without replaying the transaction**. Its entry feedback is silent on hydration. The invitation therefore remains functional independently of fresh install presentation.
- `/syncAnchors/2` and `/syncAnchors/3` bind fault-reviewed to the actual core interaction and return-chosen to the explicit F commit. The latter releases the home quotation; fault review does not change it. `/guidance/objectives/1` preserves that voluntary choice. None of these clauses requires another installation.

## Required invariant and evidence distinction

Eligibility, actual activation and audible acknowledgement are distinct. A restored transaction must not be represented as a fresh installation to satisfy ordering. Equally, its ineligible live acknowledgement must not become a permanently pending prerequisite for silent steady entry or subsequent real F actions. Already-earned review/choice state restores without falsely replaying its action; a new eligible interaction retains its signed anchor. No missing receipt, core, actor/world condition or player action may be supplied by this interpretation. Return-chosen still releases home score through the existing authority; travel remains with the world conductor.

The verifier's summaries support an observed separation: the home run reached real review/return progression with an empty home anchor ledger, while the survey run recorded repeated-measure. The home loop stopped at the return-beat predicate at 2777 ms; its later hatch anchor is a separate capture-window issue. Those observations do not justify VF-ANCHOR-OBS-1's conclusion that **all four** home anchors should be observable only during a continuous journey. Only the fresh install event requires that live boundary. The evidence does not itself prove an audible failure: local score dispatch can continue despite rejected AV activation, and no listening occurred here.

Source risk: `noteAnchor` records its local once-latch before calling AV activation and does not consume its returned success value. `activateAnchor` rejects later anchors while an earlier required same-beat anchor remains pending. `enterCommonGroundBeat` requests home-steady on entry, while `tickCommonGroundEntry` calls reactivation before requesting cell-installed. If entry callbacks run before that latter request, the live path can also reject and locally spend home-steady before installation activates. This is an entry-order/latch risk requiring continuous-path evidence, **not an observed continuous-journey failure**.

## Amendment disposition

**No creative contract amendment is required for a bounded eligibility/wiring correction that enforces these existing clauses.** Preserve real event causality, silent restoration, one live install acknowledgement, subsequent actual anchors and existing release behavior. This interpretation prescribes no code and does not waive unrelated anchor ordering, receipt or production-boundary requirements. It neither closes the verifier finding nor establishes implementation success.

# Interim verification checkpoint — Common Ground (ch13)

**This is an interim failure checkpoint, not final chapter verification.** It is
not a scorecard, not a creative judgement, and not a publication decision.
Machine-readable twin: `verification-lifecycle-interim-report.json`.

- Role: independent story-verifier. **No game source was edited.**
- Contract: scene-v2, sha256 `4dbf722b308b92b170313285854e3c9c2abac853b3407bf3e0f4efccfddff88e`
- Source manifest: `58f275f6130914f878942774fd4b4c6ce74327755c33ae257965a9dbeed40e70`
  — all **96 files independently rehashed, 0 mismatch, 0 missing**
- Preview: root-owned `http://127.0.0.1:43617/`, index sha256
  `1f327268…c05b823a`, bundle `/assets/index-CVcXc2R8.js`
  (`c34f1850…c36fca9d9`), verified to contain the repair identifier
  `railTraversal` and the exact signed marker labels
- Renderer: `ANGLE (NVIDIA Corporation, NVIDIA GB10/PCIe, OpenGL 4.5.0)` —
  **real hardware, headed**, each probe under a non-blocking `flock` on the
  shared heavy lock, released on exit

## Verdict

**FAIL (interim).** The repaired build passes every static gate and the ch13-home
interaction repair genuinely holds — but two blocking runtime defects stop the
chapter before any route traversal can be measured at all.

## What passes

| gate | result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm --prefix main run verify` | **exit 0** — 348 test files, **3026 tests**, build ok |
| `creative:gate --phase implementation` | exit 0 — **1708 checks** |
| `story:ux:check` | exit 0 — 9 files / 94 tests |
| changed-source tests (`commonGround*`, `autopilot`) | exit 0 — 13 files / 212 tests |
| six registry/journey/authority/creative/accept smokes | all exit 0 |

Static and CPU only. It proves nothing about rendering, traversal, hearing,
hardware or the movie bridge — and both blockers below are invisible to it.

**CG-IMPL-004 is not reproducible.** On hardware, `ch13:home:review` entered at
7 ms with the exact signed label and work order, was performed through the
**shared** performer (`interactionTrace` source `resolver-perform`, outcome
`returned`, prompt cleared in 0 ms), `ch13:home:choose-return` followed at
2165 ms, and the beat advanced at 2777 ms — 0 nudges, 0 page errors. The
pre-repair capture sat on that same objective for the full 300 s.

Also confirmed: every objective observed carried its **exact** signed marker
label and work order, including the scene-v2 *preparation* conditional copy for
`ch13:common:reciprocal` verbatim; and when Terra's body was 0.38 units from
W-7744 he **held** rather than displacing her (0 teleports), consistent with the
signed rule — observed in a synthetic state, so an observation, not proof.

## Blocker 1 — VF-DEEPLINK-1: the chapter boots aboard the ship

`?story=ch13-survey&movie=1` boots the player **inside the landed Kestrel** and
can never recover. 243.2 s of exactly zero displacement: body frozen at
`[8, 53.85, -6]`, `walkedPathUnits 0.000` over 2237 samples, W-7744 mounted 44 m
away, `spaceFlight {phase:'surface', controlMode:'flight'}` in **every** sample
(the module default is `fps`). The rail is alive and asking correctly
(`routeAction 'walk'`, clock 3.1 → 238.3 s) — on-foot walk simply does nothing in
flight control mode. 0 nudges, 0 page errors, 0 acts attempted.
`post/survey-movie-1/0039-root-checkpoint.png` is shot from inside the cockpit;
the debug HUD reads `Ship: landed`, `Flight: surface / flight`.

Source candidate (read-only): `commonGroundRailPlan()` has an `exit-ship` branch
only under `case 'ch13-return'`; the `ch13-survey` and `ch13-common` cases never
inspect `controlMode`.

## Blocker 2 — VF-RAIL-2: she stands on the mark she cannot reach

With an explicitly labelled disembark fixture applied, the chapter came alive —
`anc.cg.repeated-measure` at 3.3 s, the offer performed,
`anc.cg.demonstration-opened` at 13.8 s, **58.6 real units walked**. Then it
stopped for the remaining ~286 s at `ch13:survey:start`.

| quantity | value |
| --- | --- |
| player body **centre** y | 52.79–52.80 in all 2643 samples |
| authored `CG_POSES.S` | `(-26, 51.05, 12)` |
| min 3D distance, **centre** → S | **1.745** (horizontal 0.13) |
| derived **feet** y (centre − 1.3 − 0.5) | **50.99** — within **0.06** of the authored ground plane |
| distance, **feet** → S | **0.143** |
| rail gate | `CG_RAIL_START_AIM 0.35 + CG_RAIL_ROUTE_ARRIVE 0.35 = 0.70` |
| resolver reach | `CG_POINT_REACH 2.0` — satisfied by 1.745 with 0.255 margin, which is why the prompt shows |
| time standing on the mark | 261 of 354 pose-ledger entries (~4.5 min) |
| live prompt throughout | `F | Begin recording your route` |
| acts performed | **0**, with 0 teleport nudges |

`post/survey-diag-1/0038-strip-ch13-survey.png` shows the marker reading
**`survey start · begin a route · 0m`** with the F prompt on screen.

**Reconciled against the real body, as root asked — and it sharpens rather than
dissolves the finding.** `getPlayerWorldPosition()` returns the Rapier capsule
*centre*; `EfficientPlayer.tsx:1525` itself derives feet as centre − half-height.
Her feet are on the authored plane. The body *has* arrived; only the comparison
frame disagrees. **This is a coordinate-frame (centre-vs-feet / vertical
inclusion) mismatch, not a too-tight radius.** How to reconcile it is the
integrator's decision — widening radii would mask it and could relax genuine
physical clearance rules.

Why 3026 tests miss it: `commonGroundDirector.test.ts:99` `standAt()` places the
world position at the authored pose y — **a body of zero height** — so every rail
regression runs at vertical offset 0. Gates below the live 1.745 offset:
`CG_RAIL_ROUTE_ARRIVE 0.35`, `CG_RAIL_POSE_ARRIVE 0.6` (offer-span at E),
`CG_RAIL_START_AIM+ARRIVE 0.70`, `CG_RAIL_CORNER_OVERSHOOT 0.6`.

## Open anomaly for the same pass — VF-ANCHOR-OBS-1 (revised)

I **withdraw** my earlier inference that all four ch13-home anchors are provable
only in a continuous journey; Score's interpretation rejects that reading and I
accept the correction. Only `anc.cg.cell-installed` needs the live install
boundary. So the fact that deep-linked ch13-home performed both real F acts and
set both milestones while `activationHistoryAnchorIds` stayed empty in-loop is an
**anomaly**, not expected behaviour.

Source candidates, unconfirmed: `noteAnchor()` latches `runtime.firedAnchors`
*before* calling `activateSignedSceneAnchorById` and discards its boolean, so a
rejected activation is spent locally and never retried; and `activateAnchor()`
refuses an anchor while an earlier pending ordered same-beat anchor is
unactivated. Not proven — I did not instrument the return value. **No audibility
claim:** nothing was listened to, and Score rightly notes local score dispatch
may continue despite a rejected AV activation.

Separately, the empty `anchorLedger` in `home-movie-2` is a capture-window
artefact, not missing instrumentation: the loop exited on its `--until-beat`
predicate at 2777 ms and `anc.cg.hatch-boarded` activated after that. Anchor
capture demonstrably works elsewhere.

## What was NOT measured — and is therefore NOT claimed

- **The CG-IMPL-005 ordered-cursor repair in a browser.** No route traversal was
  ever entered. Retarget-to-visited-start, corner shortcuts, the ordered 18
  units, long-vs-short route classes and first-try-legal long success: **all
  unmeasured**.
- **Manual-corner deviation and recovery — not reached.** The
  `commonGroundRoute.ts:444-479` projection risk stays a source/test risk,
  deliberately kept separate from the two measured blockers.
- Three cold focused journeys; both route classes; the continuous
  station→home→ch13 bridge; the full story movie from the beginning.
- The 28 anchors as a set; the 17+2 objective lifecycles end to end; the 8-trigger
  reset matrix; mobile / reduced-motion / lowest-tier; pause / focus / quit /
  deep-link / replay.
- Any performance, fps, draw-call, memory or timing figure.
- Any score, cue, spacing or release behaviour. **Nothing was listened to.**
- The headed `chapter:evidence` bundle for chapter13.
- The typed final artifacts (`verification-report`,
  `objective-lifecycle-evidence`, `chapter-journey-evidence`,
  `raw-audiovisual-evidence`, `evidence-registry`) are **deliberately not
  authored**: filling their schemas now would mean writing booleans without
  measurements.

## Prerequisite fixtures (labelled, and not journey evidence)

`post/survey-diag-1` and `post/common-diag-1` each pressed the shipped ordinary
disembark key once (`KeyF`, `App.tsx:1516-1525`), only because the entry had
booted aboard the ship, recorded with before/after state in
`summary.prerequisiteFixtures`. It grants no milestone, position, progress or
route credit. **Those two runs are diagnostics — not cold journeys, not
continuous proof, and are not reported as either.**

## Integrity

No game source edited. No threshold or predicate changed. No teleport, progress
grant or timeout-as-rescue anywhere. No unrun check marked passed. No creative
judgement offered. Pre-repair captures and `verifier/logs/verify.log` preserved
untouched; all new evidence lives under `verifier/captures/post/` and
`verifier/logs/post-repair/`. No server was started or orphaned by this role; the
root-owned preview at `http://127.0.0.1:43617/` is root's and remains running.

Raw media inventories with per-file sha256 are in the JSON twin, kept separate
from this prose so a blind viewer can receive only the media.

All 96 signed source files still hash-identical after every probe; old captures preserved; root's preview untouched and serving. Ending the role as instructed.

## VERDICT: **FAIL (interim checkpoint)** — not final chapter verification

The repaired source passes every static gate, and the ch13-home interaction repair genuinely holds. Two **blocking runtime defects** stop the chapter before any route traversal can be measured, so the CG-IMPL-005 repair remains **untested in a browser**.

### Major findings

**Passes.** `npm run verify` exit 0 — 348 files / **3026 tests** / build ok; `creative:gate --phase implementation` 1708 checks; `story:ux:check` 94 tests; changed-source tests 212. Readiness gate satisfied and **96/96 signed source files independently rehashed, 0 drift**. Preview identity verified myself (title, index hash, and the served bundle actually containing `railTraversal`).

**CG-IMPL-004 not reproducible** on hardware: `ch13:home:review` at 7 ms with exact signed copy, performed through the **shared** performer (`resolver-perform`, prompt cleared 0 ms), choose-return at 2165 ms, beat advance at 2777 ms, 0 nudges/errors — versus the pre-repair 300 s stall.

**Blocker VF-DEEPLINK-1** — `?story=ch13-survey` boots **inside the landed Kestrel**: 243 s stall, `walkedPathUnits 0.000`, `controlMode 'flight'` in all 2237 samples, rail asking `walk` the whole time. Cockpit frame with `Ship: landed` proves it. `commonGroundRailPlan()` has an `exit-ship` branch only for `ch13-return`.

**Blocker VF-RAIL-2 (new, ≠ 004/005)** — with a labelled disembark she walked 58.6 real units to the survey start, then stood on it for ~4.5 minutes with `[F] Begin recording your route` live and never acted. Reconciled against the real body as you asked, which *sharpened* it: her **feet** are 0.143 from S (capsule centre − 1.3 − 0.5 = 50.99, within 0.06 of the authored plane), but the rail compares the **capsule centre in full 3D**, giving 1.745 against a 0.70 gate. A **coordinate-frame mismatch, not a tight radius** — I prescribe no fix. The 3026 tests miss it because `standAt()` places a **zero-height body** at the authored pose y.

**VF-ANCHOR-OBS-1 revised** — I withdraw my "all four home anchors are continuous-only" inference per Score's binding reading; the missing home-steady/fault-reviewed/return-chosen is now an **open anomaly** with two unconfirmed source candidates. No audibility claim anywhere — nothing was listened to.

**Not measured, not claimed:** all route traversal and the 18 units, both route classes, manual-corner recovery (never reached), three cold runs, station→home bridge, full story movie, 28 anchors, variants, reset matrix, any fps/timing, any audio. The five typed final artifacts are deliberately **not** authored rather than filled with unmeasured booleans.

### Artifacts
`verification-lifecycle-interim-report.{json,md}` · `verifier-findings.json` (blockers bundled for one pass) · `verifier-progress.md` · captures `verifier/captures/post/{home-movie-2,survey-movie-1,survey-diag-1,common-diag-1}` (per-file sha256 in the JSON) · logs `verifier/logs/post-repair/` · probe `verifier/probes/cg-journey-probe.mjs` (self-test passes). Pre-repair evidence untouched.

### Preview ownership
`http://127.0.0.1:43617/` is **root's** (exec session 9968), still running and usable for review — my exit does not stop it. I started no server and orphaned none. No source edits, no teleports, no timeout dressed as success. Independent re-verification of the changed source is still required; publication not authorized.
